# FutureTask

`FutureTask` wraps a computation in a `Runnable` that also provides a `Future`
handle. A bare `Runnable` has no built-in way to retrieve a result or observe
cancellation; `FutureTask` records the outcome for a caller to inspect. It can
run in a `Thread` or be submitted to an executor, but does not start itself.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- retrieve a result or task failure through `get()`;
- distinguish cancelling a future, interrupting its runner, and interrupting a
  thread waiting in `get()`;
- explain the visibility guarantee of `Future.get()` and why cancellation does
  not establish that the runner has terminated.

## Prerequisite

Install an
[Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8) JDK
or newer and ensure `java` and `javac` resolve to it in the terminal running
this example.

## The program to inspect

The program runs five `FutureTask` instances in separate threads. The first
returns `42`; the second throws an exception, which `get()` reports through
`ExecutionException`. Calling `get()` can block the caller; a timed overload is
available when an indefinite wait is unsuitable. `isDone()` also reports
completion after failure or cancellation, not just success.

The program attempts to cancel the third task with `cancel(true)`. If it
succeeds, a subsequent `get()` throws `CancellationException`, and interruption
is requested for the runner if it is running. Cancellation can fail if the task
has already completed. Interruption is cooperative: a cancelled future can be
done while its runner is still executing. Join the runner when its termination
matters.

The fourth task’s runner is interrupted directly. Ordinarily its sleep throws
`InterruptedException`, so the computation fails and `get()` reports an
`ExecutionException` whose cause is that exception; the future is not thereby
cancelled. The logged interrupt status belongs to the thread calling `get()`,
not the worker.

The fifth task has a separate thread retrieve its result. Interrupting that
thread ordinarily causes its `get()` to throw `InterruptedException`; it does
not stop the computation. The program then cancels the task and joins its
runner. It also joins the result-retrieving thread. The started and ready
latches coordinate setup, but do not prove that a worker is already sleeping or
the getter is already blocked when interrupted. A sufficiently delayed signal
can arrive after a task finishes, changing the observed outcome. These latches
support the demonstration and are not part of `FutureTask` itself.

| Concern               | `FutureTask`                                                      | Bare `Runnable`                                             |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Result and completion | `get()`, `isDone()`, and `isCancelled()` expose the outcome       | No result or completion handle                              |
| Task failure          | `get()` reports failure via `ExecutionException`                  | Reporting depends on the executing thread or executor       |
| Execution             | Pass to a `Thread` or `Executor.execute()`                        | Pass to a thread or executor                                |
| Cancellation          | `cancel(true)` attempts cancellation and may interrupt the runner | No cancellation handle; the runner can still be interrupted |
| Waiting               | `get()` may block                                                 | No equivalent operation                                     |

```java
package demo;

import java.util.concurrent.*;

import static demo.utils.CountDownLatches.await;
import static demo.utils.Logs.*;
import static demo.utils.Threads.sleepForAFewSeconds;

public final class Main {

    public static void main(final String[] args) {
        logHeaderAndJavaVersion("FutureTask");

        /* Create a FutureTask with a Callable */
        logSection("Run a FutureTask");
        log("Use Callable to run a future task and obtain the result");
        final Callable<Integer> callable = () -> {
            log("Running...");
            sleepForAFewSeconds();
            return 42;
        };
        final FutureTask<Integer> futureTask1 = new FutureTask<>(callable);
        new Thread(futureTask1, "FUTURE_TASK_1").start();

        try {
            final int value = futureTask1.get();
            log("The value returned by future task 1 is: " + value);
        } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting for future task 1 to complete", e);
        } catch (final ExecutionException e) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Future task 1 failed", e);
        }


        /* Handle errors */
        logSection("Handle errors");
        log("Handle ExecutionException when the task fails (throws an exception)");
        final FutureTask<Integer> futureTask2 = new FutureTask<>(() -> {
            log("Running...");
            throw new Exception("Simulating errors!!");
        });
        new Thread(futureTask2, "FUTURE_TASK_2").start();

        try {
            final int value = futureTask2.get();
            log("Future task 2 will always fail and it will not return a value (" + value + "), thus this message should not be printed!");
        } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting for future task 2 to complete", e);
        } catch (final ExecutionException e) {
            log("Failed while running future task 2 (" + e.getMessage() + ')');
        }


        /* Cancel long running tasks */
        logSection("Cancel tasks");
        log("Handle CancellationException when the task is cancelled");
        final CountDownLatch futureTask3Started = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final FutureTask<Integer> futureTask3 = new FutureTask<>(() -> {
            log("Running...");
            futureTask3Started.countDown();
            TimeUnit.SECONDS.sleep(20);
            return 42;
        });
        new Thread(futureTask3, "FUTURE_TASK_3").start();

        await(futureTask3Started);

        log("Cancelling future task 3");
        futureTask3.cancel(true);

        try {
            final int value = futureTask3.get();
            log("Future task 3 will always fail and it will not return a value (" + value + "), thus this message should not be printed!");
        } catch (final CancellationException e) {
            log("Cancelled while running future task 3 (Thread interrupted: " + Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() + ')');
        } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting for future task 3 to complete", e);
        } catch (final ExecutionException e) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Future task 3 failed", e);
        }


        /* Interrupt long running tasks */
        logSection("Interrupt tasks");
        log("Handle ExecutionException when the thread is interrupted");
        final CountDownLatch futureTask4Started = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final FutureTask<Integer> futureTask4 = new FutureTask<>(() -> {
            log("Running...");
            futureTask4Started.countDown();
            TimeUnit.SECONDS.sleep(20);
            return 42;
        });
        final Thread thread4 = new Thread(futureTask4, "FUTURE_TASK_4");
        thread4.start();

        await(futureTask4Started);

        log("Interrupting future task 4");
        thread4.interrupt();

        try {
            final int value = futureTask4.get();
            log("Future task 4 will always fail and it will not return a value (" + value + "), thus this message should not be printed!");
        } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting for future task 4 to complete", e);
        } catch (final ExecutionException e) {
            /* Interruptions and wrapped within the ExecutionException */
            log("Failed while running future task 4 (" + e.getMessage() + " - Thread interrupted: " + Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() + ')');
        }


        /* Interrupt while retrieving a result */
        logSection("Interrupt while retrieving a result");
        log("Handle InterruptedException when the thread retrieving a FutureTask result is interrupted");
        final CountDownLatch futureTask5Started = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final FutureTask<Integer> futureTask5 = new FutureTask<>(() -> {
            log("Running...");
            futureTask5Started.countDown();
            TimeUnit.SECONDS.sleep(20);
            return 42;
        });
        final Thread thread5 = new Thread(futureTask5, "FUTURE_TASK_5");
        thread5.start();
        await(futureTask5Started);

        /* Wait for the value within another thread, which we will then interrupt */
        final CountDownLatch getValueThreadReady = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final Thread getValueThread = new Thread(() -> {
            getValueThreadReady.countDown();
            try {
                final int value = futureTask5.get();
                log("Future task 5 will always fail and it will not return a value (" + value + "), thus this message should not be printed!");
            } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                log("Interrupted while waiting the future task 5 to complete (as expected)");
            } catch (final ExecutionException e) {
                /* Interruptions and wrapped within the ExecutionException */
                throw new RuntimeException("Future task 5 failed", e);
            }
        });
        getValueThread.start();

        await(getValueThreadReady);

        log("Interrupt the thread retrieving the future task 5 result");
        getValueThread.interrupt();
        try {
            log("Waiting for the value thread 5 to complete");
            getValueThread.join();
        } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting for the thread to complete", e);
        }

        log("Cancelling future task 5");
        futureTask5.cancel(true);
        try {
            log("Waiting for future task 5 to complete");
            thread5.join();
        } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting for future task 5 to complete", e);
        }

        log("Done");
    }
}
```

## Relation to the Java Memory Model (JMM)

The JMM defines rules for visibility and ordering of shared state. The `Future`
API specifies that actions taken by the asynchronous computation happen-before
actions following the corresponding `Future.get()` in another thread. In the
first task, this supports visibility of the completed computation’s actions to
the caller after it retrieves the result. The example does not use separate
shared data to demonstrate this guarantee.

Do not infer that cancellation waits for the runner or publishes actions it may
perform afterwards. `FutureTask` does not provide mutual exclusion for arbitrary
shared state or make compound updates atomic. Sleep and log timing do not
establish the happens-before relationship; log order can depend on scheduling.

Run these commands from the `examples/future-task` directory. Choose one of the
following ways to run the example. Observe the result, failure, cancellation,
runner interruption, and interrupted result retrieval in turn. Output timing and
the order of logs from different threads can vary.

   ./mvnw clean compile exec:exec
